chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Lu: Danny gives out information for nothing; send a bill
summary: Lu complains Danny helps foreign visitors and researchers without pay, and Milt tells him to send a bill for services rendered.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: He gives people ideas and tells them what to do, you know, and then he don't get no recognition. They're calling here and asking him things... He'll give it to them over the telephone for nothing. Never see the people no more, never hear of them or anything, you know. People

called him and never ...(?)... again. So I told him to stop all that. Sometime before I could stop him, you know, I'll still be asking, 'Are they going to pay you for that?' Right there, I shut him up.
That's right. That's what Mona does to me.
I tell him, 'You should charge for that.' But it's too much... All his life he's given out information. In New York, they were always calling him up and asking him to (?) somebody.
On these (?) shows, these foreigners, they call me to take them around...
Any time they want something, you know, for Jazz, they call him. But they don't send him no checks.
They should put you on expense(?). Send them a bill next time, Danny. Just send them a bill. Because you don't do anything for nothing. Just send it when it's over. Go and do it, and do it well.
Write (?) a letter and ask them...

Do it well. And if possible, see if you can ask whoever the dignitaries are you are (?) to say 'Would you mind dropping a letter saying whether you enjoyed my speech or not? Did you like this? Or would you sign this thing if it was okay?' And then send them a letter. These (?) probably would be delighted to write a letter. You even

took me around one time down here, with ...(? )..., and showed us all through the district. You took a bunch of us around one year. I think that way that... Maybe you could leave just a little bill for services rendered.
Well, all kinds of people come in on (?).
Surely. I know that you've been doing it as long as I've been knowing you.
